chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hajjal, from Thalabah, from Muammar ibn Yahya, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the menstruating woman who becomes clean at Asr; should she pray the first [prayer]? He (peace be upon him) said: 'No. Rather, she should pray the prayer for which she was clean.'
ai.seo_question: What prayers must a menstruating woman make up if she becomes clean during the Asr time?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the principle of 'Qada' (making up missed prayers) for a menstruating woman who regains purity during the Asr time window. Imam al-Baqir (AS) specifies that she is exempt from making up Dhuhr and only prays the single Asr prayer, establishing that the obligation attaches to the time of purity rather than the missed duration. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that menstruation suspends the prayer obligation entirely, meaning the specific missed prayer is not 'caught up' if the next prayer time begins before she performs her Ghusl.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hajjal, from Sa’alba, from Muammar Bin Yahya who said,

‘I asked Abu Ja’farasws about the menstruating woman becoming clean during Al-Asr, ‘Should she pray the former Salaats?’ Heasws said: ‘No. But rather, she should pray the Salaats which there was cleanliness with her’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hajjal from Tha’labah from Mu’ammar ibn Yahya who has said the following: “I once asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a woman experiencing Hayd (menses) becomes clean at the time of al-‘Asr must she perform al-Salah (prayer) before (al-‘Asr)?
He (the Imam) said, ‘No, she is required to perform only al-Salah (prayer) in the time of which she has become clean.’”
